title: Apple's Foldable iPhone Will Run iPad-Like Layouts and Bring Back Touch ID
excerpt: The device opens to iPad mini size with side-by-side apps, drops Face ID for a fingerprint sensor, and could cost up to $2,500 when it launches this September.
body:
• Apple's first foldable iPhone, expected this September, will feature iPad-style multitasking with side-by-side apps when unfolded, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.
  • The device will replace Face ID with Touch ID built into the power button — the first flagship iPhone to use fingerprint authentication since the iPhone X launched in 2017.
  • When unfolded, the display will be roughly the size of an iPad mini with a 4:3 aspect ratio; when closed, it will resemble a standard iPhone.
  • Pricing is expected between $1,800 and $2,500, making it the most expensive iPhone Apple has ever sold.

Apple is preparing to enter the foldable smartphone market with a device that blends iPhone portability and iPad-like productivity, according to multiple reports citing Bloomberg's Mark Gurman and analyst Ming-Chi Kuo. The device, internally referred to as the iPhone Fold, is expected to debut alongside the iPhone 18 Pro lineup in September.

An iPhone That Opens Into a Tablet

When closed, the foldable will look and function like a standard slab-style iPhone, with a compact outer display for handling quick tasks. When opened, it will reveal an inner screen roughly the size of an iPad mini, with a wider 4:3 aspect ratio designed for multitasking, video watching, and productivity.

The device will run iOS rather than iPadOS, but Apple is introducing new interface layouts that allow users to run two apps side-by-side on the larger screen — a first for any iPhone. Many apps will feature sidebars on the left side of the display, and Apple is giving developers tools to adapt existing iPhone apps for the expanded canvas.

Touch ID Returns, Face ID Goes

In a reversal that may surprise longtime iPhone users, Apple is dropping Face ID from the foldable in favor of Touch ID integrated into the side power button — the same design currently used on iPad Air and iPad mini models. According to Gurman, the front panel is too thin to accommodate the Face ID sensor array.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=6zopA-ih_ig

The outer display will use a small hole-punch camera for selfies instead of the pill-shaped notch, though Apple's Dynamic Island feature will remain for Live Activities and notifications. Apple tested an under-display camera for the inner screen but reportedly abandoned it due to poor image quality, opting for a visible camera cutout instead.

Kuo estimates the device will measure between 4.5 and 4.8 millimeters thick when opened, featuring a titanium chassis with liquid metal hinges and a virtually crease-free inner display thanks to a metal plate that distributes bending stress.

Camera Compromises and Premium Pricing

Space constraints in the foldable design mean the rear camera system will feature two lenses rather than the three found on current iPhone Pro models. Both rear cameras are expected to use 48-megapixel sensors.

The device will carry a significant price premium. Kuo projects pricing between $1,800 and $2,500, which would make it Apple's most expensive iPhone by a wide margin. For context, the current iPhone 17 Pro Max starts at $1,199. The foldable would compete directly with Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold series, which currently starts at $1,799.

What to Expect

Apple is expected to announce the foldable iPhone alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max next month. Mass production is planned for the second half of 2026. The device represents Apple's answer to a category that Samsung, Google, and other Android makers have occupied for years, though Apple appears to be betting that its wider aspect ratio and iPad-like software experience will differentiate it from existing foldables.
